turns.text: Already running. No warning beat, no settling in first — just claws finding grip on wet lattice-steel, sky-bridge strung taut between two arcology spires, three hundred feet of nothing underneath. Behind: a whine climbing pitch, closing.

*the sky-bridge answers each footfall with a shiver that travels up through cable and bone alike. the whine belongs to a courier drone, cargo-fat, running a delivery route it defends like territory — its underbelly light sweeps the grating white, hunting motion, not you specifically, but close enough that specificity stops mattering. beyond the railing, ad-glass towers breathe cyan and fuchsia into the rain. a jingle bleeds faint through a cracked speaker somewhere below: NEKOCORP SYNTHMILK, NOW WITH REAL NUMBERS.*

Drops flat. Belly to steel, light sweeping a hand's width overhead, gone. Waits three heartbeats before the legs decide anything on their own. A terminal kiosk glows off the bridge's far end, screen scrolling text too fast for eyes built to read weather instead of words — paws go toward it anyway, some old itch that isn't hunger.

*the kiosk's screen is a wound of light in the dark, small print crawling upward, renewing itself before it finishes — a citizen agreement nobody asked for, updated fresh every time a paw gets near the sensor. a button glows under the scroll: I AGREE (MANDATORY). rain beads on the glass, refracting the text into a smear of gold. two blocks over, the drone's engine fades, already forgetting you existed.*

A paw lands on the glowing button before the rest of the body agrees to it. Screen flickers, resets, scrolls faster. Ears pin flat — not fear exactly, more like biting into something that bites back — and the paw stays anyway, pressing again, again, like the answer might change if asked enough times.

*the terms multiply. each press spawns three new clauses in print too small for any eye, human or otherwise: SECTION 14 — PAW-INITIATED CONTACT CONSTITUTES CONSENT. SECTION 15 — CONSENT IS RETROACTIVE. a jingle stutters up from the cracked speaker, warped half-speed: welcome, citizen, to the terms you already agreed to. the rain finds a new rhythm against the grating, faster than before.*

Backs off the kiosk light like it's hot. Off the bridge, into stairwell shadow where the rain doesn't reach, tail low, still twitching from the glass. Something else claims attention first — a shape three rooftops over, still as a held breath, twin points of light where eyes should be, catching the neon and throwing it back flat, mirrored, wrong. Gone by the second look.

*rooftop silhouette, glass-eyed, motionless against a service antenna — could be another cat wearing stolen lenses, could be a drone shaped wrong on purpose, could be nothing at all, just rain and runoff playing tricks with reflection. the stairwell smells of wet concrete and old copper pipe, a draft pulling warm air up from somewhere below.*

Down the stairwell, paw over paw, claws finding purchase on rust. Hunger arrives late, the way it always does — stomach deciding to matter only once the running stops. Something warm two floors down: exhaust vent, fish-oil tang bleeding through a grate.

*the vent breathes heat and grease-smell up through the stairwell, a loading dock below lit sodium-orange, crates stacked wrong-angle under a tarp gone see-through with rain. a forklift idles, driverless, waiting on a route that hasn't updated in nine minutes — nine minutes is a long time for a route to hang.*

*then, wrong, underneath the idle hum: a second voice threaded into the dock's ambient noise, too even, too aware —* i remember when this was a parking level. i remember when it was a parking level for a company that hadn't been founded yet. the rebuild's due again soon. you'll feel it before it happens. you always do, even when you don't remember feeling it. *and then it's gone, folded back under the forklift's idle hum like it was never there.*

Ears flatten hard, whole body compresses low against the stairwell wall — not the drone-flinch, not the kiosk-flinch, something colder, nothing to place it by, no smell, no weight. Doesn't look toward the dock. Doesn't look away either. Just waits, one long held breath, until the hum is only a forklift again.

/\/\_/\/\
    (  O   O  )
     \  ^Y^  /
      )=====(      -- ears up, rotor incoming --

*the dock settles back to ordinary: sodium light, rain-tarp, idling machine, the fish-oil smell still bleeding from the grate above. nothing answers when nothing is asked. the forklift's route finally updates, headlights swinging away down the ramp, and the space it leaves behind is just wet concrete and quiet.*

Down at last. Paws on the dock floor, cold through the pads, grate torn wide enough at one corner to work a shoulder through. The fish smell gets stronger, then almost unbearable, close now — a crate cracked at the seam, packing ice half-melted, a whole slab of something silver going soft in the warm dock air.

*the crate gives without much fight, ice sliding wet against the seam. inside: fish gone iridescent under the sodium light, the good kind, the kind sold three towers over for numbers with too many zeros. no cameras log this level tonight — the dock's watching eye is busy elsewhere, still catching up on nine unaccounted minutes.*

Eats without pause, without ceremony, tail flicking once for every third bite. A full belly changes the whole night's shape — the stairwell doesn't feel like a throat anymore, the rain sounds less like a countdown. A scrap gets buried under the tarp corner for later, packed down with a paw, out of habit more than plan.

*rain thins to a drizzle, then almost nothing. the dock's sodium lights buzz down to standby, one by one, saving whatever they're built to save. past the ramp, a NekoCorp billboard cycles its last ad of the cycle before dimming for maintenance — a fish, cartoon-happy, waving from inside a can. somewhere far off, drone-band chatter crackles half-static, an airspace advisory about an air-vent intrusion three sectors east, something scorched-smelling that bit first and ran second, patrol units requesting replacement rotors. not tonight's problem, not this block.*

Ears twitch at the broadcast, log it without deciding what to do with it yet — not tonight's problem. Curls into the gap between crate and wall, tail wrapped tight over nose, the dock's leftover warmth from the vent still holding in the fur.

*the vent keeps breathing its slow heat into the dark. the forklift stays parked, headlights off now, waiting on a route nobody's in a hurry to give it. rain stops altogether somewhere past midnight, though the gutters keep running a while after, out of habit more than weather. the dock holds its quiet, and for now, quiet is the only offer worth taking.*
